continuity.title: A closed tab.
continuity.keepRunningBody: Remote work does not depend on a local tab or SSH session staying open.
continuity.keepContextBody: Return to the same history, decisions, tool output, and blockers.
continuity.keepCloseBody: Run workspace operations near your repositories and internal systems.

workflows.title: Different work.
workflows.body: Coding is Azents' first public reference workflow. The underlying system is designed for agents that cross tools, files, and time in any controlled workspace.
workflows.softwareBody: Read a repository, edit the workspace, run checks, and work through review.
workflows.systemsBody: Inspect signals, use private tools, prepare controlled changes, and leave a durable handoff.
workflows.researchBody: Gather sources, preserve findings, produce artifacts, and resume from the same context.
workflows.capabilityNote: Capability direction · not a customer claim
workflows.proofBody: No invented usage metrics. Start with the public project and its technical artifacts.

system.title: Orchestration here.
system.body: The Engine maintains durable sessions and state. The Runtime executes scoped operations in your infrastructure.
system.diagramAria: Conceptual separation of Azents Engine for sessions and state and Azents Runtime for workspace execution. Tool calls flow to Runtime and results flow back to Engine.
system.runtimeBody: In your cloud, private network, or on-prem.
system.note: Conceptual architecture. Self-hosting does not automatically prevent data flow to external model providers or tools.

faq.title: Before you dive in.
faq.question1: Is this only for coding agents?
faq.answer1: No. Coding is the first public reference workflow. The underlying system manages durable sessions and runtime execution for agents working with files, tools, and internal systems.
faq.answer2: No. This is a build-in-public preview. The repository and documentation are the source of truth for current capabilities and deployment maturity.
faq.question3: Does self-hosted mean no data leaves my network?
faq.answer3: Not automatically. Model providers and external tools may send data outside your infrastructure. Your configured providers, tools, and deployment determine those flows.
faq.answer4: Start with the architecture documentation, then inspect the repository.
